findings.location: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. findings.location: Ίνα διδάσκωσι τας νεωτέρας γυναίκας νηφαλιότητα, να αγαπούν τους άνδρας των, να αγαπούν τα τέκνα των –Τίτον 2:4. Η λέξη «love» στο to love their husbands σημαίνει «να τρέφουν στοργική στοργή προς τον άνδρα τους» σε σύγκριση με τη λέξη «love» στο to love their children που σημαίνει «να έχουν μητρική στοργή προς τα παιδιά τους».
findings.source_quote: That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children –Titus 2:4. The word “love,” in to love their husbands means “to be affectionately fond of their man” as compared to the word “love” in to love their children which means “to have a maternal fondness for one’s children”.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the quoted English single words and in-text quoted terms into Greek (both the Scripture citation and the explanatory occurrence of the word “love”). Replace the English word «love» with the Greek equivalent (e.g., «αγαπούν») and translate the quoted English glosses into Greek (e.g., «η λέξη “αγαπώ” στο ‘να αγαπούν τους άνδρες τους’ σημαίνει…»). Ensure all quoted material appears in Greek, matching the printed English meaning.
